neighbours.label: number-theory content about primes and divisibility (prime, composite, factors) in its mathematical sense
fire: Every even number greater than two is the sum of two primes, or so Goldbach guessed.
The teacher asked whether 91 is prime or composite.
Euclid proved that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
A perfect number equals the sum of its proper divisors, like 28.
Twin primes such as 11 and 13 differ by exactly two.
To test whether n is prime, check divisors up to its square root.
Fermat's little theorem says a to the p minus a is divisible by p.
The number 60 factors as two squared times three times five.
quiet: Every even number greater than two can be halved without a remainder.
The teacher asked whether the triangle is acute or obtuse.
Euclid proved that the angles of a triangle sum to two right angles.
A perfect score on the exam earned her a scholarship.
The prime minister met the twins at the airport.
To find the slope of the line, divide rise by run.
The rental property in a prime location sold quickly.
The number 60 appears on the bus that goes downtown.
